testimonials.summary: Shared by the women and families we serve
testimonials.title: Voices of Our Community

textblock.body: Founded in Mississauga, Crowned Women and Family Community Services was born from a vision to uplift women and strengthen families through empowerment and leadership. We believe every individual possesses a crown of worth, and our mission is to help them discover and claim it through culturally responsive support and advocacy. Over the past three years, we have served approximately 1,450 people annually, providing economic opportunities, mentorship, and health and wellness programs. Our journey is defined by a commitment to dignity and purpose, ensuring that our community thrives through the collective strength of our women and youth.

textblock.body: Crowned Women and Family Community Services was born from a vision to uplift women and strengthen families through empowerment and leadership. We believe every person carries a crown of worth, and our mission is to help them claim it through culturally responsive support and advocacy. For over three years we have served approximately 1,450 people annually with mentorship, economic opportunities, and health and wellness programs. Our work is guided by dignity and purpose, so that women, girls and families across Mississauga and the surrounding region can thrive together.

items.answer: Women, girls, youth, newcomers, couples, and families in Mississauga and the surrounding region. All backgrounds are welcome, and our programs are culturally responsive.
items.question: Who can access Crowned Women services?

items.answer: Most programs are offered at low or no cost thanks to community partnerships. Any fees are explained clearly before you begin.
items.question: Is there a cost to participate?

items.answer: Submit an intake request through our contact form or call us. We will follow up to explore available support and eligibility with you.
items.question: How do I request counseling or mentorship?

items.answer: Our team works with interpreters and culturally responsive partners so that language is not a barrier to care.
items.question: Do you offer support in other languages?

items.answer: Yes. Schools, settlement agencies, and community partners can refer women, youth, and families directly to our programs.
